changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from CV Intoxicating Substances Reference: NMDA-antagonist dissociatives (ketamine/PCP, DXM, nitrous oxide) and serotonergic hallucinogens (classic psychedelics vs NBOMe designer analogs).

summary: Two families that overlap in street use but not in danger. NMDA-antagonist dissociatives produce vertical/rotary nystagmus, dissociation, and (PCP especially) violent agitation; nitrous oxide's real hazard is a functional B12 deficiency causing subacute combined degeneration. Classic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, mescaline) have a near-zero direct-toxicity record — but NBOMe compounds sold as "acid" are a genuine toxicologic emergency.
whyThisMatters: The clinical failure modes are opposite ends of a spectrum: treating a self-limited classic-psychedelic panic reaction as a medical emergency, versus treating an NBOMe or synthetic-cathinone presentation as "just a bad trip" when it is a stimulant-hallucinogen hybrid that has killed patients despite aggressive care. And nitrous-oxide myelopathy is missed for weeks because the serum B12 is often normal and the drug is invisible to tox screens.
clinicalTakeaway: Check for vertical or rotary nystagmus — it is the fastest bedside clue to the dissociative class. Manage dissociative agitation and emergence reactions with a quiet low-stimulation environment plus benzodiazepines. For classic psychedelics, a calm room and reassurance ("talk-down") outperforms medication for most presentations; escalate to benzodiazepines only for agitation that does not settle, and reconsider the substance (NBOMe, adulterant) or an unmasked psychiatric illness if the course is severe or prolonged. Treat a "bad acid trip" with seizures, hyperthermia, severe hypertension, and rhabdomyolysis as NBOMe until proven otherwise — aggressive benzodiazepines, cooling, IV fluids. Start empiric high-dose IV B12 for suspected nitrous-oxide subacute combined degeneration without waiting for a level or MRI.

rows: Vertical or rotary nystagmus + dissociative/catatonic state (most other intoxications give horizontal nystagmus if any). PCP: prominent, prolonged, violent, unpredictable agitation (added dopaminergic/sigma activity). Emergence reaction — bizarre behavior/psychosis specifically during recovery. Chronic ketamine → ulcerative cystitis (dysuria, frequency, hematuria)

Quiet, low-stimulation environment; benzodiazepines for agitation or significant emergence phenomena. Supportive care for hypertension/tachycardia (usually self-limited). Severe refractory agitation → antipsychotics or, rarely, airway control. Evaluate a chronic ketamine user with dysuria/hematuria for ketamine cystitis, not routine UTI
NMDA antagonist (morphinan, negligible mu activity at misuse doses) + serotonin reuptake inhibition → real serotonin-syndrome risk, especially with MAOIs/SSRIs. Dose-dependent dissociative "plateaus"
Supportive care, benzodiazepines for agitation. Screen for serotonin syndrome with co-ingested SSRIs/MAOIs → benzodiazepines, cyproheptadine if refractory, stop serotonergic co-meds

Weak NMDA antagonist / GABA-A modulator, rapid on/off. Real hazard: irreversibly oxidizes the cobalt in vitamin B12 → functional B12 deficiency. Subacute combined degeneration (ascending paresthesias, gait ataxia, absent reflexes over days-weeks) in a young person with a NORMAL-to-borderline serum B12. Not on tox screens. Closed-space use → asphyxiation risk

Acute: remove from exposure, supportive observation, assess for hypoxia. Suspected SCD → empiric high-dose IV B12 without waiting for confirmatory testing (irreversible injury risk with delay); MRI spine may show cord signal change but a normal MRI does not exclude it

Low acute medical toxicity — no documented LSD fatality from direct pharmacologic toxicity. Most ED visits are acute anxiety/panic ("bad trip"), trauma from impaired judgment, or unmasked psychiatric illness. True serotonin toxicity uncommon alone (reported with LSD + serotonergic antidepressants)

"Talk-down" in a calm, low-stimulation environment is first-line and resolves most presentations without medication. Benzodiazepines for agitation/anxiety unresponsive to reassurance. Screen for trauma and co-ingestants — abnormal vitals are rarely from the psychedelic itself. Prolonged psychosis → psych evaluation, consider an alternative diagnosis or a misrepresented substance

Full 5-HT2A agonist with far greater affinity than LSD; sold on blotter AS LSD. Stimulant-heavy toxidrome: tachycardia (~62%), hypertension (~52%), hallucinations (~81%), agitation, seizures, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, and death (9 fatalities in a 42-case review). A patient who believes they took "acid" but has seizures, hyperthermia, severe hypertension, and rhabdomyolysis almost certainly did not — this is essentially diagnostic of NBOMe. Toxic leukoencephalopathy on imaging in severe survivors

Aggressive benzodiazepines for agitation, seizures, hypertension/tachycardia — a stimulant-hallucinogen hybrid, not a "wait it out" bad trip. Active cooling; IV fluids for rhabdomyolysis. Treat any suspected NBOMe presentation as a serious toxicologic emergency from the outset — status epilepticus, severe hyperthermia, and multi-organ failure have been fatal despite aggressive care

body.text: A normal serum B12 does not rule out nitrous-oxide cord disease — it is functional cobalamin activity, not the serum level, that is impaired. Treat the clinical syndrome and start B12 while workup is pending. Separately: "bad acid trip" with seizures and hyperthermia is a red flag, not a description — real LSD essentially never does this.
